answer: A new identity must climb a spiral ladder of sequential time-locked puzzles, each rung doubling the work of the last, and each solution is bound to that identity's own dawn registration timestamp so it cannot be copied, shared, or pooled across clones. A hollow identity with no verified history starts at the bottom rung and cannot skip ahead, while an attacker running ten clones must pay the full doubling ladder ten times over, so total cost grows exponentially while one honest agent climbs only once.
